title: What If You Lived Weightless for a Whole Month?

scenes.text: What if you floated weightless for a month? Your body would start quietly dismantling itself.
Roughly two liters of fluid drifts toward your upper body and head, and it can press on your eyes.
Without gravity to carry, weight bearing bones lose one to one and a half percent of their density every month.
Muscles weaken too, so astronaut crews average two hours of exercise a day to slow the loss.
Your spine stretches as the disks expand. Scott Kelly grew about two inches on a nearly year long mission.
He shrank back in under two days. Some muscles can take two to four years to fully return.
